why: Yahoo tests whether Google Publisher Tag loads. When it doesn't, Yahoo's ad-recovery loader (s.yimg.com/du/site/) goes to a numbered-subdomain video-ad player that is re-hosted on a new domain whenever one is blocked: about 1,100 more requests and a second of main thread in 12 s of scrolling. Allowing this one script is the whole fix (ddmin over the 20 hosts Yahoo has blocked: securepubads.g.doubleclick.net alone). The ad requests themselves stay blocked by the lists' host rules.

Both sites test whether AdSense's library loads, together with Criteo's (next entry). When either fails they start an ad-recovery player from numbered subdomains of a throwaway domain (about 100 requests each from 8 hosts), and allrecipes' own video player dies (JW Player error 101102). ddmin over the hosts each site blocks: exactly these two. The ad requests stay blocked.
The second half of the pair above: Criteo's prebid adapter, fetched as a test by both sites.

Tasty's recipe video is played by Connatix's player (class cnx-video-tag), which the lists block as an ad platform: with it blocked the page has no video element at all (3 of 3 passes; 8 elements and a playing video without the blocker). Found by allowing Connatix's hosts for tasty.co, then dropping to these three requests; with only the player script, the player's code (next two entries) is blocked and it still fails. The player's own ad and tracking calls (capi.connatix.com, ad exchanges) stay blocked: with these three the page has the one content video and not the ad slots.
Connatix's player code, in a versioned directory (p/<build>/...), so the prefix, not a file.
